questions.q: A customer table has 10 million rows and 300 changed today. What does change data capture (CDC) send to the other system?
options: All 10 million rows, so nothing is missed
Just the 300 rows that changed
A summary count of how many rows changed
Only the rows added, never edits
questions.explain: A nightly batch job copies all 10 million rows again. CDC asks what happened since it last looked and copies the 300.

questions.q: Log-based CDC works by reading what?
options: Copies of every table, taken once an hour
Small scripts you add to each table
A column that says when each row last changed
The database's own diary of changes
questions.explain: Databases keep a log of the changes made to them. Log-based CDC reads that log, so it doesn't need to keep asking your tables.

questions.q: Someone permanently deletes a row in the source database. Which approach is least likely to notice?
options: Timestamp (query) based CDC
Log-based CDC
Trigger-based CDC
They all notice equally well
questions.explain: A timestamp query looks for rows with a recent 'last modified' time, and a deleted row is simply gone, so there is nothing to find. Log-based and trigger-based methods see real deletes.

questions.q: Your team can't get access to the database's change log, but every table has a reliable 'last modified' column. What's the simplest fallback?
options: Give up on copying changes
Compare full copies of the database every day
Timestamp (query) based CDC
Add a trigger to every table
questions.explain: A 'last modified' column is the simplest fallback when you can't read the log. Remember it can't see real deletes, and it scans rows each run.

questions.q: Which of these is a myth about CDC?
options: It always needs Kafka
It can be set up to copy only what changed
It can capture deletes
It can send the same change twice after a crash
questions.explain: CDC doesn't need Kafka. Kafka is one place to send changes, and Debezium documents a Server mode that runs without it. Repeats after a crash are real, which is why the destination has to cope with duplicates.
